context: An elderly couple chats over morning tea
purpose: Teach: 尻/舌/裸/途端/ご存じ/突っ込ん/わざと/いまいち

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: いまいち腰の調子が良くなくてな。
lines.en: My lower back hasn't been quite right lately.
lines.style: Quiet, matter-of-fact acceptance. Light sigh underneath. No complaint—just stating what is. The tone of someone who's made peace with small inconveniences.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 昨日、椅子から尻ずらした途端、痛そうだったわよ。
lines.en: I saw you wince yesterday the moment you shifted off that chair.
lines.style: Gentle observation, no judgment. Warm noticing—the kind that comes from years of living alongside someone. Soft landing on the memory.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ご存じの通り、舌もよく噛むようになった。
lines.en: And I'm biting my tongue more often these days too, if you hadn't noticed.
lines.style: Dry self-deprecation with underlying kindness. Slight pause after 'these days'—acknowledging the small absurdities of aging without making a show of it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お医者さんに、わざと無理しないでって言われたでしょ。
lines.en: The doctor told you to stop pushing yourself so hard, didn't he.
lines.style: Steady, matter-of-fact reminder dressed as a question. Not nagging—just holding the boundary with quiet firmness. A statement more than an interrogation.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: うん。庭に出て裸足で土を踏むのが、何より効くんだが。
lines.en: Yes. There's nothing quite like stepping on bare earth in the garden—that helps more than anything.
lines.style: Contemplative, almost distant. Slow, grounded pace. Words arrive like someone remembering something true. Warmth in the simplicity.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 転んで突っ込んで怪我しないようにね、見守ってるから。
lines.en: Just don't take a tumble and hurt yourself—I'll be keeping an eye on you.
lines.style: Affectionate vigilance wrapped in lightness. Protective without fussing. The last phrase trails softly, like a promise quietly made. Warmth in every syllable.
